title: Eddie Durham and the electric guitar
summary: He praises Eddie Durham as the first to bring the electric guitar into focus, recalls his amplifier being stolen in Baltimore, and Benny Morton's arrival.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: But prior to that time before we added Benny Morton in '37, Eddie Durham had left Jimmy Lunceford and joined us in '37...
What did he join you as, a trombone player?
...playing outside of - trombone and guitar because that was his forte.
Did you have a guitar player?

Yes, we had Freddie Green. But Eddie Durham was the first one to be the innovator. He was the first man in the whole world to bring the electric guitar into focus. Nobody had never knew about electric guitar until Eddie Durham went down to a concern in Philadelphia and made them - with his steel guitar, he put the electric on it. He's the first one in the whole world to bring the innovation of an electric guitar. There never was no electric guitar in the whole world. Eddie Durham was the innovator. I think it was the Vega people, because I remember that when we got to Baltimore, they stole his amplifier and his guitar, but the 40 thieves got the guitar

back for us before we left to go to Washington, because we stopped back stage - you know how it was back stage in the theatre, at the Royal - and we were on our way to Washington. But however, Eddie Durham didn't stay with us too long because after Eddie left, then that's when Benny Morton came in. He got to came in the latter part of 1937 because Benny Morton was on recordings with - because Miss Billie Holiday was already in the band, you see, and Benny Morton was doing a thing before we went on the tour. I think I have it in my bag - at the same precise year that he joined, and by that time...
'37, the latter part of '37. Benny was with us in the first part of 1938.
